text.insert: Every app you click around in uses one shell: a collapsible sidebar, a sticky topbar, and the page content in a lane, a capped content width. An optional inspector panel docks on the right. The shell comes from the budget app,
. Its sizes are the budget sizes rounded to the 4px grid, and its colors, type and radius are the design-system tokens.

One rule ties the sidebar numbers together:
, so 68 = 2 × 24 + 20. If you change one of these tokens, keep the rule true.
Each icon starts 24px from the sidebar edge in both states, which centres it in the 68px rail. Nothing jumps when the sidebar collapses.
The toggle and the footer avatar share one centre line, 2px before the icon centres. Centring them exactly needs an off-grid 18px padding,
The shell also reads shared tokens for surfaces, text, lines, fills, type, the avatar, shape, motion and lanes.
To change a size for one app, override the token on the shell, never with a literal in a component.

/* A docs tree needs a wider sidebar. */
.docs-app.ds-shell { --ds-layout-sidebar-width: 288px; }
Thirteen numbered behavior rules fix how the shell acts. Other guide pages cite them by number, such as rule 12.
Rules 1 to 5 cover the sidebar toggle, the collapsed rail and how the app keeps the sidebar state.
The toggle is the last item in the sidebar header, at its right end.
The glyph is a panel outline with a divider and a chevron. The chevron points left (collapse) when expanded and right (expand) when collapsed.
Never put the toggle in the topbar. Never hide the sidebar completely, because the rail stays.
Labels, the title and the footer text fade out and clip under the rail edge. Subnavs and nav headings are removed.
The row of the section that holds the current page takes the fill, because its subnav is hidden.
The toggle ends up in the rail, on the footer avatar's centre line.
